mainTopic: Throwing in the sea and in swamps, carrying between boats, and drawing sea water onto a boat on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of רבא's ruling that a thrown object creates liability only once it actually lands. מרימר explains that this teaches something new, because an object flying close to the ground is sure to land, unlike a rolling object. A new משנה teaches that throwing four אמות in the sea is פטור, but throwing four אמות in a shallow swamp that the public walks through is חייב. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions 'swamp' twice. רבא says it covers summer and winter, אביי says it covers even a wide swamp, and רב אשי says it covers even a very narrow one. רב אשי's view fits his own ruling about bridge beams. A second משנה rules that throwing between sea, land and boats is פטור, and that one may carry between boats only if they are tied together. The גמרא then brings a dispute about how to draw sea water onto a boat on שבת. רב הונא requires only a small projection, while רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא require a four-by-four area. Each view is challenged and defended, ending with the rule that the Sages did not forbid indirect force (כחו) in a כרמלית. A ברייתא is brought as proof, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't this already our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא challenges רבא's ruling. Our משנה, as explained by רבי יוחנן, already says a thrown object only counts once it lands on something.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that exactly our משנה? And רבי יוחנן said about it: the thrower is liable only when the object came to rest on top of something.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of רבינא's question to מרימר. He asks why רבא needed to teach that an object must actually land, since we already know it from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא ruled that an object thrown four אמות in רשות הרבים does not create liability until it actually rests, even if it flew within three טפחים of the ground. רבינא points out that רבי יוחנן already said a rolling object must rest on something. So רבא's ruling seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as our משנה? (a challenge that a ruling is redundant)
On top of something (any surface, however small)

phrases.english: Isn't that our Mishnah,
and Rabbi Yochanan said about it:
phrases.notes: Refers to the earlier משנה about an object that rolled after being thrown.

phrases.english: and that is only when it came to rest on top of something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (previous passage) of רבא's ruling about a thrown object within three טפחים of the ground.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the object must actually come to rest.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: the משנה with רבי יוחנן's explanation already teaches that liability requires actual resting.

steps.title: A rolling object is different from one flying close to the ground
steps.stepSummary: מרימר answers: a rolling object may never stop, but an object within three טפחים of the ground is sure to land soon. So you might think it already counts as landed. רבא teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר said to him: You are talking about a rolling object? A rolling object will not necessarily come to rest. But this object will definitely come to rest soon. So I might have thought that even though it has not landed yet, it is treated as if it landed. רבא teaches us that it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: מרימר defends רבא. He shows that רבא's case is different from the משנה's case, so רבא's ruling teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rolling object might keep going, so of course it does not count until it stops. An object flying within three טפחים of the ground is about to land for sure, so one might treat it as already landed. רבא's חידוש is that even this does not count until it actually rests.

keyTerms.meaning: It is treated as if it rested

phrases.english: He (Mareimar) said to him: You are talking about a rolling object?
A rolling object will not necessarily end up resting,
but this one, since it will end up resting,
phrases.notes: "This one" is an object passing within three handbreadths of the ground.

phrases.english: even though it has not yet rested,
I might say it is like something that has rested;
so he teaches us (that it is not).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (showing the ruling adds a new point)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An object certain to land soon counts as already landed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even an object certain to land does not count until it actually rests.
steps.whatToRemember: An object must actually land to create liability. Being sure to land soon is not enough.

steps.title: משנה: throwing in the sea versus throwing in a shallow swamp
steps.stepSummary: Throwing four אמות in the sea is פטור. Throwing four אמות in a swamp less than ten טפחים deep, where the public walks, is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who throws an object four אמות in the sea is exempt. If there was a swamp and the public walks through it, one who throws four אמות within it is liable. How deep is this swamp? Less than ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It contrasts the sea, which is not רשות הרבים, with a shallow swamp that people walk through, which is רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sea is a כרמלית, so moving something four אמות there is no Torah violation. A shallow swamp that the public walks through counts as רשות הרבים even though walking there is hard. So throwing four אמות in it is like carrying four אמות in the street.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the sea counts as רשות הרבים just because it is public. It is a כרמלית, which is why the thrower is פטור.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ הַזּוֹרֵק בַּיָּם אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת — פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who throws four cubits in the sea is exempt.
If there was a swamp,
and the public domain passes through it,
one who throws four cubits into it is liable.
And how deep is a swamp?
Less than ten handbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sea is פטור; a swamp under ten טפחים deep that the public walks through is רשות הרבים, so throwing four אמות in it is חייב.

steps.title: משנה repeats the swamp ruling
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the swamp rule a second time, in almost the same words.
steps.simpleTranslation: A swamp that the public walks through: one who throws four אמות within it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the swamp case. This repetition sets up the גמרא's question about why it is said twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new seems to be added here, so the repetition looks extra. The גמרא will explain that each mention covers a different case.

phrases.aramaic: רְקַק מַיִם וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְהַלֶּכֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: A swamp that the public domain passes through,
one who throws four cubits within it is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רְקַק מַיִם וּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים מְהַלֶּכֶת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ruling of step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing four אמות within a public swamp is חייב (repeated).

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'swamp' twice?
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks רבא: the double mention of 'walking' teaches a lesson, but why mention 'swamp' twice?
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the Rabbis said to רבא: I understand why 'walking' is mentioned twice. It teaches that walking done with difficulty still counts as walking, but using a spot with difficulty does not count as using it. But why do I need 'swamp' said twice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by challenging the wording of the משנה. One repetition is explained, but the other seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repeated 'the public walks through it' teaches that even hard walking, like wading through a swamp, makes a place רשות הרבים. Awkward use of a spot, however, does not count as real use. That explains one repetition, but the word 'swamp' itself still appears twice for no clear reason.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable that... (sets up a contrast)

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: GEMARA: One of the Sages said to Rava:
Granted, 'passing,' 'passing' is mentioned two times;
this teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: הִילּוּךְ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק — שְׁמֵיהּ הִילּוּךְ,
phrases.english: passage under difficulty is considered passage,

phrases.aramaic: תַּשְׁמִישׁ עַל יְדֵי הַדְּחָק — לָא שְׁמֵיהּ תַּשְׁמִישׁ.
phrases.english: but usage under difficulty is not considered usage.
But why do I need 'swamp,' 'swamp' two times?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the repetition in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The double mention of רקק in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Extra wording: one repetition has a purpose, but the other seems pointless.
steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes a key rule: hard walking still makes a place רשות הרבים, but awkward use of a spot does not count as use.

steps.title: רבא: one is for summer, one is for winter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that one mention covers summer and the other covers winter.
steps.simpleTranslation: One mention is about the summer, and one mention is about the rainy season.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short answer: each mention of 'swamp' covers a different season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By pairing each repetition with a season, רבא makes the extra word meaningful. The next step explains why both seasons need to be taught.

phrases.english: One is about the summer
and one is about the rainy season.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְחַד בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each repetition to a different case
steps.terutzMaskana: Each mention teaches a different season.

steps.title: Why both seasons need to be taught
steps.stepSummary: Each season has its own reason people walk through the swamp, so neither case can be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If only one had been taught, I would have said the rule applies only in summer, because people walk in the water to cool off, but not in winter. And if it had taught only winter, I would say people don't mind because they are already muddy, but not in summer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why both cases are necessary, using the standard 'צריכותא' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In summer people choose the swamp to cool down. In winter they are already dirty from mud, so they don't mind. Each season has a different reason, so you could not learn one season from the other.

phrases.english: And both are necessary.
For if it had taught only one,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה,
phrases.english: I would have said these matters apply only in the summer,
since people commonly walk through to cool themselves,
but in the rainy season, not.
And if it had taught us only the rainy season,
I would say that since they are already dirty, they don't mind,
but in the summer, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and supports רבא's answer in step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One season could be learned from the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each season has its own reason for walking through, so both must be taught.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the swamp counts as רשות הרבים in both summer and winter, each for its own reason.

steps.title: אביי: one is for a narrow swamp, one is for a wide swamp
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the repetition differently. Without it, we might think people walk around a swamp that is four אמות wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It was needed. You might have thought this rule applies only where the swamp is less than four אמות wide. But where it is four אמות wide, people go around it. So the משנה teaches that people walk through it either way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different answer to the question of why 'swamp' appears twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of seasons, אביי divides the cases by size. A small swamp people just walk through. A wide one we might assume people avoid by walking around it. The double mention teaches that even a wide swamp is walked through, so it is still רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say

phrases.english: Abaye said: It was necessary,
since it would have entered your mind to say

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלָא הָוֵי אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
phrases.english: these matters apply where it is not four cubits wide,
but where it is four cubits wide,
people go around it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to step 5, parallel to רבא's answer in steps 6-7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning each repetition to a different case (by size instead of season)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A swamp four אמות wide is walked around, so it is not רשות הרבים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a wide swamp is walked through and counts as רשות הרבים.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three explanations of the double 'swamp': רבא says summer and winter; אביי says even a swamp four אמות wide counts; and רב אשי (next step) says even a swamp narrower than four טפחים counts.

steps.title: רב אשי: The repetition teaches that even a narrow swamp counts
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a third reason for the repeated swamp rule. Without it, we might think a swamp narrower than four טפחים is stepped over, not walked through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The repetition was needed. You might have thought this rule applies only where the swamp is four טפחים wide. But where it is less than four, people just step over it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers his own answer to the question of why the משנה mentions the swamp twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is about a very narrow swamp, less than four טפחים. One might think people simply hop over it, so it is not part of the public path. The second mention teaches that even a narrow swamp still counts as public ground.

keyTerms.meaning: It would have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)
These words apply (only in this case)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It was necessary,
because it would have entered your mind to say
these words apply where it is four (handbreadths wide),
phrases.notes: That's four טפחים, the smallest size that counts as a real area.

phrases.english: but where it is not four —
people step over it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 5, alongside רבא and אביי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity of the repetition: it blocks a mistaken assumption about narrow swamps.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A swamp under four טפחים is stepped over and so is not a public walkway.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even a swamp under four טפחים counts, because the public still uses it.

steps.title: רב אשי is consistent: the bridge beam ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב אשי holds the same idea elsewhere. Someone who throws an object onto a beam of a bridge is liable, because the public walks on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי follows his own reasoning. For רב אשי said: Someone who throws an object and it lands on a beam of a bridge is liable, because many people walk on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב אשי's answer fits another ruling of his about bridge beams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single bridge beam is narrow, less than four טפחים, yet רב אשי treats it as part of the public domain because people walk on it. This matches his swamp view: narrowness does not cancel public use.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning (he is consistent)
Many people pass through or walk on it

steps.whatToRemember: For רב אשי, a narrow spot still counts as public ground if people actually walk on it.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi follows his own reasoning,
as Rav Ashi said:
One who throws
and it lands on a beam of a bridge — is liable,
because many people walk on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9 by showing רב אשי holds the same principle elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: רב אשי's view that a narrow swamp counts as public ground.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אשי's own ruling that throwing onto a narrow bridge beam makes one liable.

steps.title: משנה: Throwing between sea, land and boats is exempt
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that throwing between the sea and land, the sea and a boat, or one boat and another is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who throws from the sea to dry land, from dry land to the sea, from the sea onto a boat, from a boat into the sea, or from one boat to another, is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists ways of throwing at sea and rules that none of them makes a person liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sea has the status of a כרמלית, an in-between domain set up by the Rabbis. Throwing to or from a כרמלית is not a Torah-level transfer, so there is no liability.
steps.confusionAlert: Exempt here means no Torah-level liability. It does not mean throwing this way is allowed from the start.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who throws from the sea to dry land,
or from dry land to the sea,
or from the sea onto a boat,
or from a boat into the sea,
or from one boat to another — is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The swamp discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Throwing between the sea, land and boats carries no liability.

steps.title: משנה: Carrying between boats depends on whether they are tied
steps.stepSummary: Boats tied together may have objects carried between them. Untied boats may not, even if they touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: If boats are tied to each other, one may carry from one to the other. If they are not tied, even though they are right next to each other, one may not carry from one to the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule about carrying between boats on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being tied is what links the boats into one unit for carrying. Simply touching is not enough, since untied boats can drift apart at any moment.

keyTerms.meaning: Adjacent, right next to each other

phrases.english: Boats tied one to the other —
one may carry from one to the other.
If they are not tied,
even though they are adjacent —
one may not carry from one to the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second rule of the same משנה, moving from throwing to carrying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tied boats may be carried between. Untied boats may not, even if they touch.

steps.title: Dispute: How to draw sea water onto a boat on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute. רב הונא says a projection of any size from the boat is enough to draw water. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא require a four-by-four טפחים area.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about a boat: רב הונא said, one extends a projection of any size from it and fills water. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say, one makes an area of four טפחים and fills water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a dispute about how a person on a boat may draw sea water on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boat is a רשות היחיד and the sea is a כרמלית, so pulling water up may look like moving it from one domain to another. רב הונא needs only a small projection. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא require a proper four טפחים frame to draw from.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion on the משנה
It was stated (an introduction to a dispute between אמוראים)
An area of four by four טפחים

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated: A boat,
Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיאִין הֵימֶנָּה זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמְמַלֵּא.
phrases.english: One extends from it a projection of any size and fills.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna say:
One makes an area of four and fills.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the boat משנה with a related practical dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב הונא: a projection of any size is enough. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא: a four טפחים area is required.

steps.title: רב הונא's reasoning: the air above the sea is a מקום פטור
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that a כרמלית is measured from the sea floor. The boat therefore sits in a מקום פטור, so no projection is truly needed. It is required only as a reminder.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, who said one extends a projection of any size and fills, holds that we measure the כרמלית from the ground, and the air above is a מקום פטור. By law a projection should not be needed at all. It is required only so that he has a sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא needs only a tiny projection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית reaches only ten טפחים up from its ground. Here the ground is the sea floor, and the sea is deeper than ten טפחים, so the water's surface near the boat is a מקום פטור. Drawing from a מקום פטור into a רשות היחיד is permitted, so the projection is just a reminder not to draw from a real כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: An in-between domain, restricted by the Rabbis
We measure from the ground (here, the sea floor)
An exempt area, where carrying rules do not apply

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the projection is not a legal requirement for רב הונא but only a safeguard. That sets up the contrast with רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיא הֵימֶנָּה זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמְמַלֵּא,
phrases.english: one extends from it a projection of any size and fills,
because he holds we measure a karmelit from the ground,
phrases.notes: Here the ground is the sea floor, more than ten טפחים below.

phrases.english: and the air above is an exempt area,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְדִין הוּא דְּזִיז נָמֵי לָא לִיבְעֵי,
phrases.english: and by law a projection too should not be needed,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא — כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֶיהְוֵי לֵיהּ הֶיכֵּרָא.
phrases.english: but rather — it is so that he will have a sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר מוֹצִיא הֵימֶנָּה זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמְמַלֵּא, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes רב הונא from step 13 in order to explain his reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For רב הונא, the area above the sea is a מקום פטור, and the projection serves only as a reminder.

steps.title: Why רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא require a four-by-four area
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא measure the כרמלית from the surface of the water. The water counts like solid ground. Without a four-by-four frame, a person would carry from a כרמלית into a רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא say: one makes a four-by-four area and fills. They hold that we measure the כרמלית from the edge of the water, so the water is treated like solid ground. If he does not make a four-by-four area, he carries from a כרמלית into a רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the other side of the dispute from Step 13. It shows why רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא need a full four-by-four area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא measured the ten טפחים from the sea floor, so the air above ten is a מקום פטור. These אמוראים instead start measuring at the water's surface, as if the water were the ground. That makes the area right above the water a real כרמלית. A four-by-four frame is needed to change that area's status.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of four by four טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that a כרמלית ends at ten טפחים. They disagree only about where you start counting: from the sea floor (רב הונא) or from the water's surface (רב חסדא).

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמְרִי
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna say:
one makes an area of four [by four] and fills,
they hold that we measure the karmelit from the surface of the water —
the water is like solid ground,
if he does not make an area of four —
he is carrying from a karmelit to the private domain.
phrases.notes: The boat counts as a רשות היחיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to Step 14: Step 14 explained רב הונא's reasoning, and this step explains the opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כרמלית is measured from the water's surface, so a four-by-four frame is required to draw water.

steps.title: Challenge to רב הונא: what if the water is shallow?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רבה בר אבוה a question about רב הונא's view. Sometimes the water is less than ten טפחים deep. Then the area above it is a כרמלית, and a tiny projection would not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רבה בר אבוה: according to רב הונא, who said one puts out a projection of any size and fills, sometimes there are not ten טפחים, and he is carrying from a כרמלית into a רשות היחיד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's lenient view. It points to cases where the sea is shallow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's leniency depends on the boat being more than ten טפחים above the sea floor, which makes it a מקום פטור. If the water is shallow, the area by the boat falls within ten. It is then a real כרמלית, and a tiny reminder-projection would not be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: There are not ten (טפחים of depth)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to Rabba bar Avuh:
And according to Rav Huna, who said

phrases.aramaic: מוֹצִיא הֵימֶנָּה זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמְמַלֵּא,
phrases.english: one extends from it a projection of any size and fills,
sometimes there are not ten [handbreadths of depth],
and he would be carrying from a karmelit to the private domain!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר מוֹצִיא הֵימֶנָּה זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא וּמְמַלֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רב הונא's view from Step 14 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a projection of any size is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reasoning only works when the water is ten טפחים deep, which is not always the case.

steps.title: Boats do not sail in water shallower than ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר אבוה answers with a tradition: a boat does not travel in water less than ten טפחים deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: we have learned that a boat does not travel in less than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. It says the shallow-water case does not really happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry assumed a boat could sit over shallow water. The answer relies on a received fact about boats: they always need at least ten טפחים of water. So רב הונא's assumption that the area is a מקום פטור always holds.

phrases.english: He said to him: We have learned
that a boat does not travel in less than ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמְרִינַן דְּאֵין סְפִינָה מְהַלֶּכֶת בְּפָחוֹת מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the problem case can happen in reality
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A boat might float over water less than ten טפחים deep.
steps.terutzMaskana: Boats never sail in water under ten טפחים, so רב הונא's view stands.

steps.title: But the front of the boat can reach shallow water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a boat has a raised front part (מורשא). That part can extend over shallower water, so the boat may still be in water under ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it has a protruding front part!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Part of the boat might still be over shallow water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule was that boats need ten טפחים of depth. But the boat's shape is not even. Its front part rises and can pass over shallower spots. So some part of the boat could stand over water less than ten deep.

keyTerms.meaning: The raised, protruding front part of a boat

phrases.english: But it has a protruding [front] part!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a boat is never in water under ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of the boat's shape, part of it can be over shallower water.

steps.title: Depth-measurers walk ahead of the boat
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that people who measure the depth with poles go ahead of the boat. They make sure the water is at least ten טפחים deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said: the depth-measurers go in front of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last challenge. In practice, the depth is checked ahead of the boat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sailors send measurers in front with long poles to keep the boat out of shallow water. So the boat, including its front, stays in water at least ten טפחים deep. רב הונא's view holds.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's lenient view works because a boat is always in water at least ten טפחים deep. Experience shows this, and depth-measurers make sure of it.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
The depth-measurers go in front of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 and closes the challenge to רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical fact that removes the problem case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The boat's front might pass over shallow water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Measurers keep the whole boat in water at least ten טפחים deep.

steps.title: How does he pour out waste water according to רב חסדא?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks: according to רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, where does the person pour his dirty water? If he pours it into the same frame he draws from, the water there becomes disgusting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רב חייא בר אבין: according to רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, who say one makes a four-by-four area and fills, how does he throw out his waste water? And if you say he throws it into that same place, it would be disgusting to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the stricter view and raises a practical problem. Pouring dirty water straight into the sea would be throwing into a כרמלית, and pouring it into the frame would spoil his drinking water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, the sea right next to the boat is a כרמלית. So pouring waste directly into it is forbidden. The one allowed spot, the four-by-four frame, is where he draws his water, so dumping waste there makes that water disgusting.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin:

phrases.aramaic: לְרַב חִסְדָּא וּלְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: According to Rav Ḥisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna,
who say one makes an area of four and fills,
his waste water, how does he throw it out?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּשָׁדֵי לְהוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם —
phrases.english: And if you say he throws it into that same place —
it would be disgusting to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from challenging רב הונא to challenging the view of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A permitted way to get rid of waste water according to the strict view

steps.title: He pours it onto the boat's side wall
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that he pours the waste onto the side of the boat. From there it runs down into the sea on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: He throws it onto the side wall of the boat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא בר אבין gives a practical solution. The person does not pour straight into the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring onto the boat's wall is not a direct throw into the כרמלית. The water flows into the sea by itself afterward. This also keeps the waste away from the frame he drinks from.

phrases.english: He throws it onto the side wall of the boat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He pours the waste onto the boat's side, and it then flows into the sea.

steps.title: But the water still reaches the sea by his force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even so, the water goes into the sea because of his pouring. That is still his force (כחו).
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is his force!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the solution. Pouring onto the side still sends the water into the sea through his action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The water flows down the wall because he poured it. An act done through a person's force is often treated as his own act. So it seems he is still moving water into a כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: His force, an indirect result of his action

phrases.english: But there is his force!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The solution of pouring onto the boat's side
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An indirect result of one's force should count like a direct act, so it is still forbidden.

steps.title: No decree against indirect force in a כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Sages did not make a decree against כחו in a כרמלית. They only forbade throwing directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For his force in a כרמלית, they did not decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the solution with a general rule about indirect force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרמלית is forbidden only מדרבנן, as a rabbinic decree. The Sages limited that decree to direct actions. They did not extend it to water that reaches the כרמלית through a person's indirect force.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule כחו בכרמלית לא גזרו is a general principle. It allows indirect actions in a כרמלית, which is only rabbinically forbidden.

phrases.english: Regarding his force in a karmelit, they did not decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rabbinic decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Indirect force into a כרמלית is just as forbidden as a direct throw.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sages did not forbid indirect force in a כרמלית.

steps.title: A ברייתא as the source for the rule about force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the rule that כחו in a כרמלית is allowed. It begins quoting a ברייתא: one may not carry from a ship into the sea, or from the sea into the ship.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you say this? As it was taught in a ברייתא: with a ship, one may not carry from inside it to the sea, nor from the sea into it,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a proof for the rule in Step 23. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the proof continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first states the basic ban on carrying between a ship (a רשות היחיד) and the sea (a כרמלית). The part that proves the rule about force has not appeared yet. It will come in the continuation of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And from where do you say this?
As it was taught: A ship —
one may not carry from inside it to the sea
nor from the sea into it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a source for the rule given in Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the Sages did not forbid כחו in a כרמלית
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about carrying between a ship and the sea (continues on the next amud)
